title: Policy adapter concurrency synchronization error causing cross-key metering inflation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Intermittent overcounting of usage is occurring when requests traverse the policy adapter under concurrent load and fallback routing. Symptoms include unexpected per-key quota throttles for healthy customers and inflated billing counters in aggregate metrics. This appears correlated with concurrent policy evaluations that race updating transient accounting structures used by the enforcement step.
observed_behavior: Under synthetic load that mimics bursty traffic (mix of short chat streams and single-shot completions) we observed per-key meter increments that exceeded the number of inbound tokens by ~18-40% for some traces. Customers reported unexpected 429s despite low steady-state usage. The console billing dashboard shows a sudden spike in token counts for affected orgs at the same timestamps.
expected_behavior: Policy adapter should increment meter only once per accepted token stream and should never attribute the same token to multiple quota buckets. Throttles should only trigger when the true aggregated usage crosses configured limits.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy a small cluster with policy-adapter running latest staging image
Run the concurrency load harness: 200 clients, 50ms inter-request variance, 15% configured fallback routing enabled
Enable detailed per-route and per-org accounting logs and ingest to dev-dashboard
Observe meter increments for a sampled org over the 10 minute run and compare inbound token estimate vs accounted tokens
impact: Affected orgs see spurious throttles leading to degraded product experience; internal billing team sees inflated token totals that may generate erroneous billing disputes. Platform reliability is impacted because enforcement decisions cascade (fallbacks trigger more retries, which cause more overcounting).
root_cause_summary: Race between the policy evaluation path and the enforcement accounting updater: when a request triggers fallback routing or concurrent retries, transient accounting entries (in-memory per-request deltas) are merged non-atomically into shared per-key aggregates. Under concurrency these merges can be applied multiple times due to retry semantics and a missing idempotency guard, leading to double-counting. Additionally, telemetry batching code batches deltas by route and flush timing mismatches can duplicate a delta if acknowledgements overlap with retry flushes.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Rate-limit control plane to reduce fallback routing frequency for the most impacted orgs. 2) Roll out a conservative shadow-mode patch that drops duplicate accounting deltas based on a generated request fingerprint to reduce immediate overcounting. 3) Notify billing ops and mark suspect windows for manual reconciliation.
proposed_fix_summary: 1) Add an idempotency token to per-request accounting deltas and enforce single-apply semantics in the aggregator. 2) Serialize the accounting merge for deltas that touch the same per-key shard using an optimized compare-and-swap path to avoid full locks. 3) Harden telemetry flush acknowledgements so deltas are not re-sent on overlapping retry windows. 4) Add integration tests that exercise concurrent fallback + retry scenarios and assert accounting invariants.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic concurrency harness produces accounted token totals within 1% of inbound estimated tokens across 1000 runs
No duplicate meter increments observed when fallback routing is enabled in the harness
PR passes unit tests, integration concurrency tests, and performance baseline (latency P95 regression < 5%)
Billing ops can run a reconciliation job that reconciles historical suspect windows and marks them as adjusted
